text: Continuous integration, or CI, is a software development practice where developers regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. Each time code is added, automated builds start immediately, compiling the project and checking that everything works together. As part of the process, the system also runs tests automatically to confirm that new changes do not break existing features. This approach helps teams catch issues early, when they are easier and cheaper to fix. A well-designed CI pipeline can build, test, and report results within minutes, giving developers fast feedback and keeping the main codebase stable and reliable.
